data.narrative:
Nuro, a Series G autonomous delivery drone company founded by Dave Ferguson and Jiajun Zhu, is evaluated against a peer set of four private and public stage drones & autonomous companies, including Zipline ($7.6B), Joby Aviation ($6.9B), Archer Aviation ($3.3B), and Elroy Air. The company's last post-money valuation stands at $6.0B against $2.2B total capital raised.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis applies a typical 1.25x step-up multiplier to the $6.0B Series G valuation, implying $7.5B. Peer-median analysis across the three most comparable companies (Zipline, Joby Aviation, Archer Aviation) yields a median valuation of $6.9B, with a range spanning $3.3B to $7.6B. These methods reflect material variance driven by valuation dispersion within the autonomous vehicle sector.

Triangulating both approaches produces a valuation range of $5.8B to $8.6B, with a median of $7.2B. This range sits 20% above the current $6.0B mark, suggesting modest upside from last round. Key uncertainties center on which peer trajectory Nuro will track—the higher-valued Zipline baseline versus the lower-end Archer comparables—and timing of next financing or exit event. The relatively tight peer dispersion ($3.3B–$7.6B) and limited method count warrant conservative reliance on this analysis pending additional operational metrics.
